title: Assignment 3: From messy export to one-slide answer
intro:
**The brief.** Your manager forwards the raw 2025 order export: "Before Monday's meeting I need one slide: **where is our revenue coming from now?** The export's a mess, so clean it first."

The export (A–H) has **11 problems of six kinds**: duplicated orders, blank regions, inconsistent region text, quantities stored as text, a mistyped product ID, and a date in the wrong year. Nobody will tell you which rows; finding them is part of the job. The reference tables in J–X are clean.

Work in the three panels below: clean, then pivot, then chart. The tasks are checked from your workspace when you submit. The pass mark is **8/8**, and you can resubmit as often as you like. Your moves are saved as you go, so a reload loses nothing.

> [!tip] A move that breaks good data (a Remove Duplicates on the wrong column, a Find & Replace with no scope) fails every cleaning task until you Undo it. And remember what the last lesson taught about pivots and data that changes.

tasks.hint: COUNTIF on the OrderID column finds them; Remove Duplicates removes them. Tick every column.

tasks.ask: **Fill the blank regions**, from each order's rep (not a guess).
tasks.hint: Find blanks in column D, then fill only the blanks with a lookup of the rep's name in Q:R.

tasks.ask: **Standardise the region names** (no stray spaces, a capital first letter).

defects.label: a region with stray spaces or the wrong case
a region with stray spaces or the wrong case
a region with stray spaces or the wrong case

tasks.hint: One formula, filled down D and pasted as values, fixes both the spaces and the case.
Look for green corners in column G.

tasks.ask: **Fix the mistyped product ID and the date in the wrong year.**

defects.label: a date in the wrong year

tasks.hint: A ProductID that isn't in the price list shows up in the pivot's note. Sorting by Date, newest first, surfaces the other.

tasks.ask: **Pivot:** Region down the side, Quarter across the top, Sum of Revenue, on the **cleaned** data.
tasks.hint: Insert it after cleaning, or Refresh it after your last cleaning move. Rows: Region; Columns: Date → Quarters; Values: Sum of Revenue; no filter.

tasks.ask: **Chart Qtr4 revenue by region** so the leader stands out: a fitting chart type, sorted, with a title that states the finding.
tasks.hint: Chart the Qtr4 series of your pivot, largest first. The title should name the region that leads Qtr4, not just describe the axes.

tasks.ask: **The one-sentence answer.** Fill in the blanks from your pivot (the share to one decimal place).

story.sentence: In Qtr4, {top} brought in the most revenue: €{amount}, {share}% of the quarter's total, while the full-year leader, {leader}, brought in only €{leaderAmount}.

amount.label: Qtr4 revenue of the leading region

tasks.hint: Qtr4's leader and its share come from the Qtr4 column (share = its cell ÷ the Qtr4 total). The full-year leader has the biggest Grand Total; read its Qtr4 cell.
